summary: Focused review of local URL routing and Firestore authorization. Tested direct unauthorized requests were denied. The score reflects an existing admin roster workflow defect, not a demonstrated URL-based privilege escalation. Live Firebase deployment and a comprehensive security audit are outside this assessment.

findings.issue: The admin dashboard offers ward setup/configuration, but wards and women permit reads only through activeClinicalMember (doctor/nurse). An admin can write ward configuration but cannot read the roster required by that UI.
findings.recommendation: Decide which roster metadata administrators should see, then align the UI and authorization rules with that policy. This change intentionally does not broaden admin permissions.

scope: Address-bar identifiers are validated and cannot provide role, access level, user identity, or organization membership.
Clinical selection uses the current organization's authorized roster and checks the admission belongs to the selected ward.
Signed-out and unverified protected routes do not render clinical content.
Local Firestore rules deny unauthorized direct reads, cross-organization reads, self-promotion, unauthorized membership changes, key grants, and ward administration writes.
Clinical read access remains organization-wide, not restricted to individual assigned wards or patients.
